title: Longest Line of Consecutive One in Matrix
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix, determine the length of the longest sequence of consecutive ones that can form a line in any direction: horizontal, vertical, diagonal, or anti-diagonal.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix, determine the length of the longest sequence of consecutive ones that can form a line in any direction: horizontal, vertical, diagonal, or anti-diagonal.
constraints: mat contains only zero and one; a line may be horizontal, vertical, diagonal, or anti-diagonal.
hints: Each one can extend four lines ending at its cell.
Remember the previous length in each direction.
For a one, add one to left/up/up-left/up-right predecessor counts.
Every maximal line has a final cell, so tracking runs ending at each cell finds the global maximum.
editorial: Every maximal line has a final cell, so tracking runs ending at each cell finds the global maximum.

tests.explanation: The best horizontal, vertical, and diagonal runs all have length three.
The two diagonal ones form a length-two line.
